The *Maṇipūjakattheraapadāna* is a verse narrative located within the *Therāpadāna* collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. The text records the past karmic deeds and devotional aspirations associated with the elder (thera) Maṇipūjaka. While no direct discussions of this poem appear in the searched secondary literature, five translations across five modern languages are indexed for it on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
SuttaCentral notes resembling parallels between this text and two versions of the *Upavānattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 24 and Tha-Ap 562), the *Sāriputtattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 3), the *Upālittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 8), and the *Mahāvāṇijajātaka* (Ja 493) [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis via DharmaNexus reveals 116 text-reuse passages shared with 28 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest internal reuse is found in the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (first volume), which shares extensive text over segments §0.3–20.1 totaling more than 4,500 characters, alongside further shared passages in the second volume of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus and SuttaCentral agree on a significant shared passage with the *Upavānattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 562, segments §11.3–12.4), while DharmaNexus additionally identifies formulaic reuse with numerous other Apadānas, including the *Ekāsanadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 425), *Gandhapūjakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 462), *Vedikārakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 451), and *Paṁsukūlapūjakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 494) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matches, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of the text with the Sanskrit *Kaṭhināvadāna* (such as segment §7.4), though this represents a machine-generated alignment rather than an established parallel [DharmaNexus].
